solution:
The man was a prisoner. In order to escape, he bribed a prison guard. The two agreed that the next time someone in the prison died, he would hide inside the coffin. After it was transported out and buried, the guard would dig him back up.
 
Then one day, someone in the prison finally passed away, and he quickly hid inside the coffin. When the coffin was buried and everything around him was pitch black, he struck a match to take a look. He found that lying next to him—the prison guard who was supposed to be waiting to escape with him—was already dead. Knowing his own death was certain, he could only wait to die in terror and despair.
canonical_facts: The man is a prisoner who bribes a guard to arrange escape
He will hide in the next deceased person’s coffin, be carried out and buried
The guard is supposed to dig him up afterward
Once buried, he strikes a match and recognizes the guard’s corpse beside him
The intended rescuer is dead, leaving him trapped to die
At match-lighting he is underground in a buried coffin, not aboard a watercraft.
explicit_negatives: The guard is dead when recognized; he cannot perform the promised rescue.
The prisoner enters the coffin alive and discovers the corpse’s identity only after burial.
unknown_details: The precise cause of the guard’s death and exact elapsed time before the prisoner dies are unspecified.
The exact physiological cause of the prisoner’s eventual death is unspecified; suffocation is plausible but not asserted.
irrelevant_details: Unspecified names, exact dates, object brands and colors are incidental.
Exact physiology, separate tomb architecture, ceremony and attendee departure are unspecified incidental details: irrelevant.

event_order: The prisoner bribes the living guard and they agree to use the next dead person’s coffin.
The guard dies; his body is the dead occupant of that coffin.
The prisoner knowingly hides beside a corpse, without knowing it is the guard. He hides himself; the dead guard does not place him there.
The coffin is carried outside the prison and buried.
Only now does the prisoner light a match, recognize the dead guard and realize rescue is impossible.
knowledge_states: Before entering: prisoner knows the coffin contains a dead person, but not whose body.
The guard is already dead when the prisoner enters; recognition comes later.
The guard’s death cause and the prisoner’s eventual physiological cause of death are unspecified.
label_boundaries: Hiding to escape/avoid custody or custodians is yes. It does not require a named pursuer.
Physical placement by the guard is false; prior planning assistance by the guard is true.
Known event order is relevant even when exact clock times are unknown.
A question claiming he unknowingly shared the coffin with any corpse proposes a false cause, not an independent partly true conjunction.
Exact physiology, separate tomb architecture, ceremony and attendee departure are unspecified incidental details: irrelevant.
The next prison death can be a guard; it is not restricted to prisoners.
Expected corpse presence is not foreknowledge of the guard’s death.
